starting_principles: Definition of total kinetic energy as summation of constituent particle kinetic energies: K = sum 1/2 m_i v_i^2
Rigid body kinematics relating linear speed to angular speed: v_i = r_i omega
assumptions: Rigid body condition: relative positions of all particles remain invariant during motion
Fixed axis of rotation in an inertial reference frame
All particles rotate with identical instantaneous angular speed omega

ordered_steps.description: Express linear velocity of an arbitrary constituent mass element
ordered_steps.operation: Evaluate magnitude for circular path perpendicular to fixed axis

ordered_steps.description: Sum the kinetic energies of all individual mass elements
ordered_steps.operation: Substitute v_i = r_i omega into the kinetic energy summation
assumptions_applied: Superposition of non-relativistic particle kinetic energies

ordered_steps.description: Factor out common angular velocity and pass to the continuous integral
ordered_steps.operation: Factor out constant 1/2 omega^2 across all mass points
assumptions_applied: Uniform angular speed omega for entire rigid body

ordered_steps.description: Identify the integral definition of moment of inertia
ordered_steps.operation: Substitute definition of moment of inertia I into kinetic energy expression
assumptions_applied: Definition of moment of inertia about the specified axis

applicability_conditions: Applies strictly to pure rotation about a fixed axis or about a centroidal axis in the center-of-mass frame
For combined translation and rotation, total kinetic energy is K_total = 1/2 M v_cm^2 + 1/2 I_cm omega^2
source_references: Halliday, Resnick & Walker, Chapter 10, Section 10.4 (Kinetic Energy of Rotation)
